title: Almond biscotti (cantucci)
summary: Twice-baked Tuscan almond biscotti with whole almonds and a hint of orange, made without butter as in Prato.
steps: Heat the oven to 165 °C (325 °F) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Whisk the almond flour, erythritol, xanthan gum, baking powder, salt and anise together.
Beat the eggs with the vanilla and orange zest, then stir into the dry ingredients to make a stiff, sticky dough. Mix in the whole almonds.
With wet hands, shape the dough into a log about 30 cm (12 in) long and 7 cm (3 in) wide, and flatten the top slightly.
Bake 25 minutes, until firm and golden. Cool for 20 minutes; almond-flour logs crumble if sliced hot.
Lower the oven to 150 °C (300 °F). With a serrated knife, cut the log on the diagonal into 24 slices about 1.5 cm (½ in) thick.
Lay the slices flat and bake 10 minutes, turn them and bake 8–10 minutes more, until dry. They crisp further as they cool.
tips: Saw gently with the knife rather than pressing down, and the whole almonds will cut cleanly.
In Tuscany they are dipped in sweet wine; coffee works too.

origin.history: Twice-baked biscuits kept well and were made in Italy for centuries; 'biscotto' itself means twice-cooked. The almond version known as cantucci or biscotti di Prato is tied to the Tuscan town of Prato, where a bakery made them famous in the nineteenth century. The traditional dough uses eggs, sugar, flour and almonds, with no butter or oil.
